evidence.ai_role: The pretrained potential supplies relaxed structures and force responses for scalable phonon screening, enabling selection of specific low-thermal-conductivity lithium binaries.
evidence.tested: MatterSim phonon screening, separate 3,558-material DFT comparison and within-study first-principles third-order force-constant/Boltzmann calculations for LiPt, LiTl and LiBi. The latter check the specific low-conductivity candidate result computationally.
evidence.unknown: No new synthesis or experimental phonon/thermal-conductivity validation is reported. Model errors, dynamic-stability filtering and gap cutoffs affect candidate counts; not every candidate receives separate DFT confirmation.

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 full HTML: Computational methods, Benchmark and validation, High-throughput calculations, Phonon gap and thermal conductivity, Origins of low thermal conductivity and Conclusions. Source header v1 date and affiliations read.

summary: A preprint used the MatterSim learned interatomic potential to calculate phonons for 42,347 stable, previously observed compounds and flag 11,176 with predicted phonon gaps larger than 1 THz. Screening and existing-database thermal descriptors prioritized lithium-metal binaries; targeted first-principles Boltzmann calculations then predicted room-temperature lattice thermal conductivities of 2.47, 0.63 and 0.33 W m−1 K−1 for LiPt, LiTl and LiBi, respectively. These are computational properties of known compounds, not new synthesis or experimentally measured performance. The large candidate list is model-derived; a separate DFT benchmark does not independently validate every screened material.
title: MatterSim screening identifies low-conductivity lithium-metal candidates
